_comment: Hermetic runner definitions for eval-triggers.sh (Step 2c).
EVERY flag here is load-bearing and was chosen from an empirical probe, not from --help.
Probe log, 2026-08-01, claude 2.1.220 on an OAuth (non-API-key) host:
--setting-sources ''   THE isolation flag. Control group proves it: WITHOUT it a --print
run quoted the host's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md rule [T0-3] verbatim AND
obeyed a sentinel CLAUDE.md planted in cwd; WITH it the same prompt
answered NO-SUCH-RULE and ignored the sentinel. Never drop it: the
eval would then be measuring the host's own config, not the skill.
--tools 'Skill'        Skill firing is a tool call, so '' (all tools off) makes firing
IMPOSSIBLE and every case silently scores 'quiet'. Exactly one tool
is exposed: the model can fire a skill or answer in text, nothing else.
--plugin-dir           The injection channel. eval-triggers.sh synthesizes a throwaway
plugin ('skilleval') because --plugin-dir wants a plugin directory
(.claude-plugin/plugin.json), not a bare skill folder.
--output-format stream-json + --verbose   The only machine-readable ground truth:
{'type':'tool_use','name':'Skill','input':{'skill':'skilleval:NAME'}}.
--no-session-persistence   Keeps 200+ eval runs out of the resumable-session store.
DELIBERATELY NOT USED:
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<empty dir>   Breaks auth on this host. Probed: the run returned
'Not logged in - Please run /login' because OAuth credentials are
keyed to the config dir (there is no ~/.claude/.credentials.json;
they live in the macOS keychain). Only safe for API-key hosts.
--bare                 Same reason: its own help text says Anthropic auth becomes strictly
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper, so an OAuth host cannot use it.
The --setting-sources flag is the one claim here that is mechanically enforced: eval-triggers.sh
refuses to run any non-mock runner whose resolved command lacks it. Everything else in this
block is documentation and does not enforce itself.
RESIDUAL CONTAMINATION, measured once and accepted — NOT re-checked at runtime:
1. Built-in skills stay loaded even at --setting-sources ''. The init event listed 18
(code-review, debug, verify, simplify, run, loop, ...). USER skills were correctly
absent. Consequence: a case whose prompt reads like 'review this code' can be won by
built-in code-review rather than the skill under test. That is a REAL collision the
audit wants to see, so it is reported (winner is always named), never suppressed.
2. Auto-memory stays enabled; memory_paths.auto is namespaced by cwd. The runner therefore
runs each case in a FRESH temp cwd, which yields an empty memory namespace. Running from
a real project directory would reintroduce recalled memories into the prompt.
COST: live runs consume the 5-hour rate-limit window (init emits a rate_limit_event).
One case is one full model turn. Use --max-cases while iterating.

claude-baseline._comment: Control arm: identical, but --disable-slash-commands turns every skill off. A case that still 'passes' here is measuring the base model, not the skill.

mock._comment: Offline runner for tests/trigger-eval.sh. Reads the prompt on stdin and emits canned stream-json, so CI exercises the REAL parser and scorer with zero API calls. What it emits is controlled by $SKILLEVAL_MOCK_MAP: a TSV of <prompt-substring> TAB <skill-name | empty | __NORESULT__>, first match wins, no match means nothing fires. mock-runner.sh holds the full contract. Exempt from the --setting-sources check because it never reaches a model. Never produces a trustworthy audit number.

_codex_deliberately_absent: There is no codex runner, and adding one would be a defect. Probed 2026-08-01, codex-cli 0.146.0.
BLOCKER — codex emits no machine-readable skill-invocation event, so there is no ground truth.
Probe: `codex exec --json` with an explicit `$deps-check` invocation and a prompt forbidding
further work. The agent replied '已載入 $deps-check；未執行任何命令' — it HAD loaded the skill —
while the JSONL stream contained only thread.started / turn.started / item.completed
(agent_message, error) / turn.completed. No tool call, no SKILL.md read, nothing naming the
skill. Contrast claude, which emits {'type':'tool_use','name':'Skill','input':{'skill':...}}.
A rejected hypothesis, recorded so nobody re-tests it: an earlier probe showed ~20
command_execution items after a skill fired, suggesting the load might BE a shell read of
SKILL.md. It is not — those were the skill's downstream work. The minimal-work probe above
produced zero command_execution items while still loading the skill.
A codex runner would therefore score EVERY case 'quiet' and report a clean sheet, which is the
exact infra-blind false pass that tests/trigger-eval.sh exists to forbid. Absence is the
correct implementation until codex exposes an invocation event.
TWO SECONDARY FINDINGS, both worth keeping even though the arm is not built:
1. UPSTREAM'S ISOLATION CLAIM IS FALSE ON THIS HOST. The i-have-adhd repo's
evals/runners.example.json runs codex as `codex exec --ephemeral --ignore-user-config
--sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check --json` and treats that as hermetic. Control
group: that exact invocation, asked about a rule that exists only in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md,
quoted [T0-3] back verbatim. --ignore-user-config does NOT drop AGENTS.md.
2. WHAT DOES WORK: CODEX_HOME pointed at a temp dir, with the real ~/.codex/auth.json
SYMLINKED in (symlink, never a copy — the file holds credentials). Same sentinel prompt
then answered NO-SUCH-RULE, and auth still worked. This is the mirror image of claude,
where CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at an empty dir breaks OAuth outright, because claude keys its
credentials to the keychain by config dir while codex keeps them in a plain file.
Not enough on its own: the ~95-skill corpus loads regardless of CODEX_HOME (the run still
warns 'Codex can still see every skill'), and a [[skills.config]] entry for a NEW skill
did not register it — a probe asking codex to list its skills never returned the injected
fixture. So even with instructions isolated, the corpus cannot be scoped to one skill,
which rules out an --isolate arm independently of the ground-truth blocker.
